key_insight: Competing Ge-driven polar off-centering and Sn-favored octahedral tilting create a low-temperature phase boundary in lead-free CsGe₁₋ₓSnₓBr₃ between x = 0.60 and 0.65.
engineering_relevance: Ge/Sn alloying offers a route to tune structural order and band gaps in lead-free perovskites relevant to solar-cell materials design.
method: Train a charge-aware machine-learned interatomic potential on hybrid-functional data.
Run large-scale molecular dynamics across the full Ge/Sn composition range.
Map composition–temperature phases and assess band-gap trends.
evidence_signal: Simulations reproduce both end members’ known transition sequences and temperatures and reveal an intermediate I4/mcm phase absent from either parent compound.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational materials predictions, not experimental alloy validation or demonstrated solar-cell performance.
paper_title: Competing Octahedral Tilting and $B$-Site Off-Centering Govern the Phase Diagram of CsGe$_{1-x}$Sn$_x$Br$_3$ Perovskite Alloys
